title: Application of Meaning-Based Psychotherapy to a Sample of Patients With Chronic Pain
official: Application of Meaning-Based Psychotherapy to a Sample of Patients With Chronic Pain
summary: The aimes of this study is to determine whether Meaning-Based Psychotherapy (MBP) is an effective therapy for improving sense of purpose, reducing depression, and improving quality of life in people with chronic pain and to verify the effectiveness of the MBP intervention for participants in a randomized controlled trial (RCT) by comparing it with the optimized usual care (Cognitive-behavioural Psychotherapy por chronic pain).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Participants will be adults;
2. Patients treated at Mental Health Service for anxiety and depressive symptoms related to chronic non-cancer pain; the diagnosis will be recorded according to the ICD-10 criteria identified in their medical records.
3. Tendency to catastrophize pain (score greater than 30 on the Pain Catastrophizing Questionnaire (García-Campayo, J., 2008));
4. Low sense of purpose or lack of a defined sense of purpose in life (score less than 105 on the Purpose in Life Test (PIL) (Crumbaugh \& Maholick, 1969).

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Diagnoses of a severe mental disorder (schizophrenia, substance dependence, dementia, or cognitive impairment) identified through information obtained in a clinical interview or digital health record.
2. Severe suicidal ideation or a suicide attempt within the last 6 months. This will be assessed using responses to item 9 of the Beck Depression Inventory (2nd ed.). This item is commonly used in clinical studies to identify suicidal ideation and has proven to be a good predictor of suicidal intent and risk (Green et al. 2015, von Brachel et al. 2018). Participants with recent suicide attempts or whose response to item 3 ("I would commit suicide if I had the opportunity") will be excluded, as this indicates suicidal intent and a higher risk of suicide (Green et al. 2015). In such cases, referral to the appropriate mental health service will be prioritized according to protocol.
